technical.summary: Severe oversold conditions with long-term bullish structure but price trapped below all moving averages, negative momentum, and no confirmation signals—high risk of further downside before reversal.

fundamental.summary: SRE shows no fundamental momentum: zero insider activity, no institutional signal, no government contracts, no lobbying engagement, minimal retail interest, and earnings in 35 days create near-term uncertainty.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (16/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but stale congressional data (695+ days old) and absent recent news sentiment provide no confirmation.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (329.92) indicates extreme market stress, strong dollar pressures multinationals, and earnings in 35 days adds event risk to utilities sector already facing credit stress.

debate.key_bull_argument: Extreme oversold RSI (23.99, 26.63) combined with contrarian fear sentiment (16/100) and long-term bullish moving average structure (EMA 20/50 and SMA 50/200 bullish) create classic reversal setup near support at 69.373.
debate.key_bear_argument: Price trapped below all major moving averages with negative MACD histogram, zero volume confirmation (OBV flat, CMF negative), no triggered strategies, zero fundamental momentum, and macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis, strong dollar) make this a bear trap disguised as oversold opportunity.

decision.entry_rationale: Extreme oversold RSI and contrarian fear sentiment present theoretical reversal setup, but price remains trapped below all major moving averages with zero volume confirmation and negative momentum—entry quality too weak to justify risk.
decision.primary_risk: Macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis, strong dollar) combined with earnings event in 35 days create high probability of further downside before any reversal materializes.
decision.agent_agreement: moderate — technical and sentiment agents see contrarian opportunity, but fundamental and risk agents strongly reject entry; debate decisively favors bear case (8 vs 4).
